question.value: Which interferometer plus single-dish data combination methods recover the true sky flux best, and how can their performance be quantitatively assessed (new A-par, fidelity, power-spectrum and spectrogram diagnostics)

evidence.quote: In this work, we provide an overview of the prominent available methods to combine single dish and interferometric observations.

This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00004.SV.

findings_qualitative.value: Interferometric filtering affects flux recovery at all scales, including compact structures comparable to the beam, not only beyond the MRS

evidence.quote: our results clearly demonstrate how the interferometric filtering has a significant impact at all scales

findings_qualitative.value: FSSC produced results nearly identical to Feather in the skymodel test

evidence.quote: The FSSC method is not shown but produced results nearly identical to Feather in this test.

findings_qualitative.value: Recovered power-spectrum values and slopes in interferometric images should be interpreted with extreme caution

evidence.quote: The physical interpretation of the recovered SPS in interferometric observations (e.g. absolute values and changes in the power spectrum slope) should be treated with extreme caution.

claims.hypothesis: Does omitting single-dish data cause significant flux and spectral-line errors in interferometric images of resolved sources
claims.experiment: Compared int-CLEAN with combined images against the true skymodel and the M100 SD cube using A-par, flux vs signal, power spectra and spectrograms
claims.result: int-CLEAN recovers ~32% of the skymodel flux and loses ~50% on average in M100 channels; combination recovers ~89-92%
claims.finding: Interferometer-only reductions can miss up to 90% of flux at all scales, and deform line profiles

evidence.quote: Interferometric-alone reductions can miss up to 90% (A-par=-0.9) of the flux depending on the scale and source morphology.

claims.hypothesis: Do the tested combination methods all improve over interferometry alone
claims.experiment: Applied Feather, SDINT, MACF and FSSC to skymodel and M100
claims.result: Feather, SDINT and MACF recover most flux with errors of about 10% or less
claims.finding: Any tested combination method is better than interferometric data alone

evidence.quote: Our results on the performance of the tested data combination methods show quantitatively that the application of any method is better than using the interferometric data on its own.

claims.hypothesis: Is any one combination method clearly superior
claims.experiment: Compared A-par statistics and spectrograms of methods on both datasets
claims.result: SDINT and MACF best on the skymodel; Feather and MACF best on M100 at SD resolution
claims.finding: Performance varies with target structure; no clear universal winner

evidence.quote: While our analysis does not allow to establish the clear superiority of any of the data combination methods in all situations

claims.hypothesis: Is the new A-par parameter a better diagnostic than Fidelity
claims.experiment: Computed both A-par and Fidelity maps and histograms for the same combinations
claims.result: A-par is signed and has a defined optimum, Fidelity is unsigned and has no target value
claims.finding: A-par has higher diagnostic value than Fidelity

evidence.quote: We also discuss the commonly used Fidelity parameter, and we find A-par to have higher diagnostic value.

claims.hypothesis: Does lacking short-spacing information distort spectral line profiles
claims.experiment: Compared M100 spectra from int-CLEAN, Feather and SDINT in two regions
claims.result: int-CLEAN spectra show negative features, reduced FWHM and shifted peak
claims.finding: Data combination is needed to preserve line fluxes and kinematic information in cubes

we therefore choose the spectrally resolved observation of the galaxy M100 as an example of real observational data

referee_caveats_inferred: Method ranking rests on one simulated skymodel and one galaxy; no repeats or uncertainty on the differences between methods
Reference for M100 is the SD cube itself, so SD calibration errors and SD-resolution averaging limit the test; ~20 voxels per channel
Method parameters (sdfactor, sdgain, effdishdiam) were not tuned, so ranking may change with tuning
M100 calibration and the origin of the SD cube are not described in the paper
Noise properties of the simulated data are not given, so noise-dependent A-par widths are hard to compare
